title: Runbook (draft): Nightly Perf Baseline Jobs (Q1 2026) — Operations, Paging, and Safe Reruns
body:
Audience: SRE on-call + perf-canary operator rotation (Q1 2026)

Purpose
- Operate the nightly Perf Baseline suite runs (aka “baseline nightly”) with predictable paging behavior.
- Distinguish real runtime regressions from noise (fleet/region drift, telemetry issues, harness flake).
- Provide a safe rerun procedure that preserves reproducibility guarantees (environment pins, artifact stamping) and avoids masking true regressions.

Scope / Non-scope
In-scope
- Nightly scheduled baseline suite run(s) across the agreed model/hardware/region matrix.
- Failure modes: infra, environment drift, data pipeline, baseline comparison, runner issues.
- Paging criteria + what to do when paged.
- Safe reruns + annotation requirements.

Out of scope
- Creating new traffic shapes or changing baseline definitions (see Runtime/Methodology docs).
- Debugging kernel/scheduler behavior beyond first-pass triage (we route to Runtime owners with artifacts).

Key concepts (operational definitions)
- “Run”: a single execution of the baseline suite for a specified matrix (model x shape x region x hardware) on a given runtime commit/build.
- “Baseline”: locked reference values for Q1 2026, versioned artifacts. Used for drift detection.
- “Drift”: measured delta from baseline beyond allowed variance budget for a metric.
- “Noise”: deltas attributable to harness flake, fleet changes, driver/CUDA mismatch, telemetry pipeline anomalies, or capacity mix.

Primary metrics monitored
(Details live in methodology docs; this is the ops view.)
- Latency
  - TTFT (Time to First Token)
  - TPOT (Time Per Output Token)
  - E2E latency (non-streaming), and streaming chunk timing where available
  - p50 / p95 / p99
- Throughput
  - tokens/sec (server-side) + successful req/sec under defined concurrency
- Reliability
  - error rate by class (timeouts, OOM, 429/load-shed, 5xx)
- Explainability signals (used in triage)
  - queue wait time distribution
  - batch composition stats (prefill/decode)
  - backpressure / load-shedding counters
  - cache hit rate / warmup phase indicators

Where to look
- Perf-canary nightly job
  - CI/CD: perf-canary scheduled workflow (see GitHub perf-canary/pr-188)
  - Artifacts: baseline-run JSON summary, per-workload raw output, environment stamp (driver/CUDA/runtime SHA), runner logs
- Dashboards (Grafana/Console)
  - Baseline drift overview by model/shape/region/hardware
  - Drilldown: run metadata + links to artifacts
  - Alert panels (warn-only as of early rollout; paging rules below)
- Telemetry validation notes
  - If TTFT/TPOT looks “too good” or “too bad” across the board, suspect ingestion/timestamp issues first

On-call responsibilities
- Acknowledge page, classify event, execute first-pass triage within 30 minutes.
- If rerun required, follow Safe Rerun Procedure below and annotate.
- Escalate to Runtime / Observability / Telemetry owners with the required packet.
- Ensure the event is logged (Slack thread link + ticket) and the dashboard is annotated.

Paging policy (current draft; subject to change with rollout)
We page only on high-confidence, high-severity signals. Everything else is a Slack notification + next-business-day triage.

P0 (Page immediately)
Page if ANY of the following are true for a baseline-critical slice (top served models/shapes) AND the system passes basic sanity checks (runner completed, env stamp present):
- p99 TTFT regression > 15% vs baseline on 2+ consecutive trials OR across 2+ regions (same hardware SKU)
- p99 TPOT regression > 12% vs baseline on 2+ consecutive trials OR across 2+ regions
- Error rate increases to > 2% for a workload slice that normally sits < 0.2% (excluding intentional load-shed shapes)
- Any workload suite slice fails entirely (runner cannot complete) AND the failure is not clearly infra-wide (e.g., general outage)

P1 (Slack notify + file ticket; no page)
- Single-region p99 regression beyond variance budget but isolated to one region or one hardware pool
- p95 regressions only, without p99 movement
- Throughput drop > 10% but without latency regression (often indicates batching/shape mismatch or capacity throttling)
- Metric pipeline anomalies suspected (missing dimensions, sudden step-changes across all models)

P2 (Log only)
- Flake signatures: transient runner errors that succeed on retry; intermittent network errors; one-off timeouts
- Small deltas within variance budget or changes confined to non-critical shapes

“Baseline-critical slice” definition (as of this draft)
- Streaming chat shape(s) + long-context streaming
- Bursty concurrency shape(s)
- Mixed prompt-length shape(s) at moderate concurrency
Note: exact shape IDs are defined in the workload suite v0; see Runtime for canonical list.

First-pass triage checklist (10–20 min)
1) Confirm the run is valid
- Runner completed? Any step skipped?
- Environment stamp present in artifacts (runtime SHA, build ID, driver, CUDA, kernel selection seed if applicable)
- Region + hardware match the expected pool
- Were there known fleet maintenance events in the time window? (check fleet notes / on-call channel)

2) Classify the failure type
A. Infra / capacity / fleet
- Symptoms: many timeouts, inability to provision nodes, widespread failures across models
- Common causes: capacity exhaustion, preemption behavior change, noisy neighbor, fleet mix drift

B. Environment drift (high priority to identify)
- Symptoms: only one region/hardware suddenly deviates; “severe regression” that disappears when run on pinned pool
- Common causes: driver/CUDA mismatch, new instance type in pool, mixed GPU stepping
- Correlate with Jira INT-1440 patterns

C. Harness / runner
- Symptoms: missing artifacts, schema changes, generator bug, bad retry behavior, run aborted
- Check runner logs; look for “config validation”, “artifact upload”, “metadata stamp” messages

D. Telemetry / metrics pipeline
- Symptoms: TTFT/TPOT shift uniformly across all slices; weird zeros; negative timestamps; missing streaming first-chunk timing
- Cross-check with client-measured timing (if available) and recent telemetry changes

E. Real runtime regression
- Symptoms: consistent delta across regions/hardware, stable across rerun, explainability metrics point to queue wait / batch composition / prefill-decode imbalance
- Escalate to Runtime with packet

3) Gather “escalation packet” artifacts (required for any escalation)
- Run ID + timestamp window
- Runtime commit SHA + build metadata (from artifact stamp)
- Hardware SKU + region + pool identifier
- Workload shape ID(s) impacted
- Before/after metrics: baseline vs current p50/p95/p99, TTFT/TPOT, error rate
- Runner logs excerpt around failures
- Dashboard link(s)

Escalation routes
- Runtime regression suspected
  - Primary: Noah Patel + Sofia Ivanova + Hiro Tanaka (depending on signal: scheduler vs kernel)
  - Include Marcus Reed for suite semantics / harness assumptions
- Environment drift suspected
  - Vanessa Ortiz (fleet/hardware normalization) + SRE on-call channel
  - File/update INT-1440 if not already tracked
- Telemetry pipeline suspected
  - Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman
- Dashboard/alerts broken
  - Sergio Costa / Allison Grant

Safe Rerun Procedure (do not skip)
Goal: rerun to confirm signal while preserving reproducibility and avoiding “moving target” inputs.

When to rerun
- Required for P0 unless the root cause is obvious infra-wide failure.
- Recommended for suspected environment drift (rerun on explicitly pinned pool).
- Optional for runner flake after fixing the issue (but annotate that the rerun is post-fix).

How to rerun safely
1) Do NOT change workload definitions or seeds
- Use the same workload suite version/tag as the failed run.
- Verify seeds/configs are identical (artifact versioning).

2) Pin environment
- Pin hardware SKU and region.
- Pin driver/CUDA image if the runner supports it.
- Ensure runtime build metadata stamping is enabled (see runtime metadata stamping PR in redwood/pr-24010).

3) Choose rerun mode
- “Confirm-only rerun” (preferred): rerun the exact failing slices (model x shape x region x hardware) with identical trial counts.
- “Full suite rerun” (only if needed): if failure indicates systemic issue (pipeline, runner) and partial rerun won’t be representative.

4) Control concurrency and warmup
- Ensure warmup/cooldown phases run as defined by methodology.
- Do not manually “pre-warm” caches outside the harness; it contaminates comparability.

5) Record the rerun and annotate
- Add an annotation in the dashboard: reason for rerun (flake/env drift confirmation/etc.).
- In the ticket/Slack thread, include original run ID, rerun ID, and whether any infrastructure pins changed.

Hard rule: never replace a failing run’s artifacts
- Store rerun artifacts as separate run IDs.
- Comparisons should reference both (original + rerun) to avoid hiding intermittent issues.

Common failure modes + signatures
1) Fleet driver/CUDA mismatch (classic)
- Signature: massive p99 jump in one region; others fine; runner stamp shows unexpected driver/CUDA.
- Action: rerun with pinned image; escalate to Vanessa + file INT-1440 update.

2) Mixed hardware pool (silent skew)
- Signature: high variance across trials; bimodal latency distributions; only on one pool.
- Action: inspect node inventory tags in run metadata; rerun on known-homogeneous pool.

3) Streaming TTFT definition/first-chunk timestamp bug
- Signature: TTFT suddenly improves/worsens only for streaming workloads; non-streaming unaffected.
- Action: check recent telemetry changes; compare server vs client timing if available; escalate to Logan/Nadia. (Known historical issue fixed in runtime PR redwood/pr-23944; ensure running post-fix build.)

4) Runner upload / artifact store partial failure
- Signature: job “green” but missing raw outputs; dashboards show gaps.
- Action: treat as failure; rerun after fixing upload; escalate to Observability if artifacts aren’t ingesting.

5) Real scheduler regression under bursty concurrency
- Signature: p99 TTFT increases; queue wait histograms shift right; backpressure/load-shed counters change; batching composition changes.
- Action: rerun confirm-only; escalate to Sofia/Julian/Noah with explainability metrics.

6) Kernel autotune nondeterminism
- Signature: prefill TPOT noise; changes correlate with kernel selection logs; high sensitivity to restarts.
- Action: verify seeds/pinning; rerun twice to gauge stability; escalate to Hiro/Yuki.

Decision tree (quick)
- Missing artifacts / runner incomplete → treat as runner failure; no regression claim; rerun after fix.
- Env stamp differs from baseline requirements → classify as env drift; rerun pinned; do not alert Runtime as “regression” until confirmed.
- Same env + reproducible delta across rerun → likely real; page/escalate per severity.

Logging requirements
- Every P0/P1 event must have a ticket and a linked Slack thread.
- Include:
  - original run ID + rerun IDs
  - classification label (infra / env drift / telemetry / runner / runtime regression)
  - owner assigned
  - next checkpoint time (e.g., “recheck after 2am rerun”)

Current open questions (TODO)
- Finalize exact P0 thresholds per metric once variance budget is locked (Sana Farid’s study).
- Confirm which slices are “baseline-critical” for paging vs notify-only.
- Decide whether to page on throughput-only regressions (currently: no, unless paired with latency or high error).
- Add a one-pager for release-train usage: what qualifies as “must-fix before ship” vs “file follow-up.”

Appendix: contacts (as of Q1 2026)
- SRE baseline ops: Sean Gallagher (primary), Aisha Bello (dashboards)
- Runtime perf architect: Noah Patel
- Scheduling/batching: Sofia Ivanova (lead), Julian Moore (instrumentation/load-shed)
- Kernels: Hiro Tanaka (lead), Yuki Sato (determinism)
- Workload suite: Claire Dubois; suite maintainer: Marcus Reed
- Telemetry: Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman
- Fleet normalization: Vanessa Ortiz
- Release qualification: Connor O’Brien; CI/nightly automation: Sahana Iyer

Last updated notes
- 2026-02-19: Added env drift / driver mismatch as explicit P0 rerun requirement; tightened rerun annotation rules; added telemetry signature section for streaming TTFT.
